assertion.text: Erdős Problem #313: declared status 'open'. Formalized: yes. Are there infinitely many solutions to\[\frac{1}{p_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{p_k}=1-\frac{1}{m},\]where $m\geq 2$ is an integer and $p_1<\cdots<p_k$ are distinct primes? Prize: no. OEIS: A054377. Tags: number theory, unit fractions.
